thread:
marta: FYI support ticket from a customer (reported via support-bot) — p95 fine but p99 jumped to ~1.2s for a 0-token generation workload around 09:12 UTC.
eli: they sent a few traces; looks like tail latency linked to batching delays. I'll paste snippets.
eli: trace snippet: 
```
request_id=abc123 stage=queue_wait wait_ms=87 batch_size=32 kernel_exec_ms=12 total_ms=1100
request_id=abc124 stage=queue_wait wait_ms=91 batch_size=33 kernel_exec_ms=13 total_ms=1210
```
marta: those waits are way above our normal queue waits (~<20ms). Sounds like batching timeout inflating.
kai: which batcher? continuous or microbatcher?
eli: continuous-batcher on inference-pool-g4. Config snapshot from yesterday: `max_batch_size=64`, `batch_timeout_ms=50`, `preferred_batch_size=8`, `enable_adaptive_timeout=true`
oliver: enable_adaptive_timeout=true might be causing overshoot under bursty small-req traffic. we saw similar last quarter.
marta: support-bot mentioned spike coincided with a short burst of 5k tiny requests from a customer feature rollout. lots of single-token prompts.
kai: single-token prompts + preferred_batch_size=8 + high max_batch_size means we wait for either batch fill OR timeout. If arrival rate is moderate, we wait close to batch_timeout_ms per request and then flush large batches -> long queue waits for earliest requests in batch -> p99.
eli: reproducer script I used: 
```
for i in {1..500}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-small","prompt":"Hi","max_tokens":1}' &
done; wait
```
results: p95 ~ 90ms, p99 ~ 1.1s when continuous-batcher left at 50ms. When I lowered `batch_timeout_ms` to 12ms in canary, p99 dropped to ~130ms. p95 slightly higher (~120ms) but still acceptable.
marta: can we confirm this without touching prod? run a canary on 2 nodes?
oliver: started a canary pool with same workload and patched config to `batch_timeout_ms=12` and `max_batch_size=32` — monitoring now.
ops-bot: deploy canary to pool inference-pool-g4-canary initiated by oliver at 09:44 UTC
kai: quick analysis of metrics: batch_size histogram skewed to high counts at flush times, queue_wait percentiles: p50=8ms p90=35ms p95=92ms p99=1050ms. CPU/GPU utilization unchanged -> not compute.
eli: logs show a pattern: small requests arrive steadily but not enough to fill preferred_batch_size quickly, adaptive timeout bumped wait to near max.
marta: short-term mitigation options?
eli: 1) lower batch_timeout_ms for affected pools (fast, immediate) 2) reduce preferred_batch_size to 4 or 2 (helps small requests) 3) enable small-request routing: tiny prompts to a fast-sync path (newer feature) 4) throttle customer rollout (support action)
oliver: I applied option 1 in canary; if stable we can rollout config change via rollout plan (canary -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%).
kai: also add a metric alert for queue_wait p99 > 300ms to catch early.
marta: support-bot — ask customer to throttle if they can and share time window. eli please attach repro script and timeline to the ticket.
eli: done, added repro and traces.
ops-bot: canary metrics update: queue_wait p99 dropped from 1050ms to 110ms on canary nodes after patch at 09:50 UTC.
oliver: Recommend global patch: `continuous_batcher.batch_timeout_ms=12`, `continuous_batcher.max_batch_size=32`, `continuous_batcher.preferred_batch_size=4` for pools serving low-token workloads. We'll run rollout over 30m.
kai: one caveat: lowering timeout increases per-token cost slightly (less batching efficiency). we should calculate cost impact. can we auto-tune by workload type?
marta: add an action to product: tag routes with workload profile (tiny/short/long) so batcher can use per-route policy. eli add that to roadmap ticket.
eli: short repro steps for on-call: 1) run reproducer above against a canary pool 2) curl canary config endpoint: `PATCH /internal/pools/{pool}/config` body: `{ "continuous_batcher": { "batch_timeout_ms": 12 } }` 3) watch `metrics:continuous_queue_wait_ms` and `metrics:batch_size_histogram`
marta: if rollout is safe, do canary -> 20% -> 100% with 10m windows. oliver take lead on rollout.
oliver: starting canary->20% at 10:12 UTC. will monitor latency, token-cost and gpu utilization.
ops-bot: rollout to 20% initiated by oliver at 10:12 UTC
kai: also add temporary alert suppression for non-customer-facing flaps for 15m during rollout.
eli: post-mortem notes: root cause = workload mismatch: bursty stream of single-token requests + adaptive timeout behavior amplified queue wait. mitigation = shorter timeouts + smaller preferred batch size for tiny workloads, plus routing.
marta: excellent. assign owners: oliver -> rollout, kai -> metrics/alerts, eli -> support ticket & repro, marta -> follow-up doc + roadmap ticket. update ticket when 50% and 100% done.
eli: quick note: if we see increased token cost > 8% on rollout, pause and switch to targeted routing instead of global timeout change.
marta: thanks team. closing loop with customer now (eli), we'll update once rollout completes. :thumbsup:
